macro_blurb: US tech sentiment is being shaped by AI monetization signals, after Workday jumped 14% on a raised margin forecast tied to AI strength, while SpaceX prepares the 12th Starship test flight against the backdrop of a potential IPO. In European consumer staples, Estée Lauder and Puig have walked away from a cosmetics tie-up, removing a prospective consolidation story from the luxury beauty space. On the regulatory front, Meta reached a settlement in a bellwether case over social-media addiction among minors, keeping platform-liability risk in focus for large-cap tech. Geopolitically, Germany's Foreign Minister Wadephul voiced concern over a Turkish court's removal of the CHP leader, adding a fresh governance overhang to Turkey-exposed European names.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a deep-value pile, and an American one. All 10 picks are US-listed, with an average Value percentile of 88.6 against a far softer Quality average of 58.3 — the algo is paying for cheapness and accepting balance-sheet question marks to get it. Momentum is the second tilt at 84.5, so what surfaces are stocks the market has already started to re-rate from low bases. Healthcare leads the sector count at 3 of 10 (CNC, DVA, CI), Consumer Defensive contributes 2 (MO, KHC), and composites are tightly bunched between 74.0 and 85.3 — no standout, a flat leaderboard.

The clearest thread runs through Healthcare: Centene, DaVita and Cigna all combine top-decile Value with strong 3-month momentum (+33%, +31%, roughly flat) against a sector that's down 9% over the same window — a managed-care and provider re-rating off depressed bases, with CNC's FCF yield at 24% and CI's trailing P/E at 2.5x flagging how distressed the entry points were. A second thread sits in high-yield Consumer Defensive: MO (5.78%) and KHC (6.8%) both screen top-decile on Yield with sub-median Quality — the classic "is the dividend real" trade.

The outlier is CF Industries — the only Basic Materials name, riding a nitrogen-price spike and an ammonia outage rather than any factor shared with the rest. The conspicuous absences matter more: Industrials, Consumer Cyclical, Utilities and Communication Services produced zero picks from 992 screened, and Technology contributes only HPQ — notable given Workday's 14% AI-driven move and the live Meta settlement keeping large-cap Tech in the headlines but out of this value-led screen. Two near-term swing factors: any softening in the Iran-driven oil bid would hit APA's momentum score directly, and further AI-monetization prints could widen the gap between this screen and the Tech tape it is ignoring.
